inspiration: Motion-command input: moves are typed as short sequences of directions with a release marker and a hold marker, and the button must be the last element. A special is a contiguous match in a short direction-and-button history (src/libopenfight/moves.cpp:11-12, 69-109). Re-express with our own notation. Shape only (LGPL-3).

Input window: each change of a key opens a 10-frame window during which the queue is kept; the queue holds up to 20 changes (src/libopenfight/playerAgent.h:19-20; playerAgent.cpp:41-65). This is the input buffer shape for the touch and lock-on forgiveness topic.

Hits resolve only when the attacker's animation frame changes, and the hit is an accepted state transition on the defender: the spark object spawns only if the defender accepts the hurt state (actions.cpp:45-48; player.cpp:158-164). A hit the defender cannot take in its current state fails quietly. Fits the hitstun eligibility shape for row 3.

Combo gate: a combo move needs the opponent's hurt flag set, and the flag clears when the hurt animation ends (player.cpp:101, 151-152). Keeps a combo window tied to the victim's animation, not a timer.
Facing mirror: one collision box is defined once and flipped by the facing flag when computing its edges (collisionBox.cpp:29-36). Saves a second set of boxes for the other facing.

Projectile as its own object: a projectile is a separate object created at the hit point, checked every tick, and reports itself done on first overlap (player.cpp:158-161, 184-195; the caller that removes it was not read). Matches the fire-and-forget bolt shape.

Pushback: when two defence boxes overlap while one fighter steps forward, the stepper recoils half the step and the other fighter is moved by twice the step (player.cpp:245-251). Only the non-inverted sign was checked.
Frame delay of 0 holds a frame until the state changes (animation.cpp:113). Useful for hold poses and charge tells.

Defects to fix, not copy: (1) Player::doAction declares an uninitialised Actions pointer, then reads it (player.cpp:203, 209-210); fix: initialise to nullptr. (2) get(current_state) is dereferenced with no null check (player.cpp:132, 269); fix: guard. (3) updateState dereferences the opponent with no null check (player.cpp:101, 120); fix: guard. (4) The 4-argument CollisionBox constructor builds a temporary instead of delegating (collisionBox.cpp:4), leaving the fields unset; fix: delegate in the initialiser list. (5) getTrigger returns the last match in passes 1-2 and the first match in pass 3 (moves.cpp:81, 109); fix: one priority rule. (6) PlayerAgent::update swaps the caller's keys array in place (playerAgent.cpp:35); fix: copy first.
No health system yet: ROADMAP.md line 9 is unchecked. The hit outcome is only a state change, so a damage model would need to be designed fresh (row 17 and 18).

briefs.label: Ember bolt (own label)
briefs.why: A ranged bolt that hangs in the air and ends on the first contact. Reads as a clear threat at 375 wide if the bolt is bright against a dark stage.
briefs.keep: Projectile is its own object; ends on first overlap; spawns at a facing-relative offset
briefs.change: Our bolt has a travel speed, a lifetime and a wind-up tell; its colour and shape are a new original design; no sprite from this donor

briefs.label: Accepted-hit spark (own label)
briefs.why: A short spark that appears only when the defender actually takes the hit, so a whiffed or blocked hit shows no spark. Gives the hit a clear feedback beat.
briefs.keep: Two-frame short-lived effect; spawned only when the hit is accepted
briefs.change: Our spark is procedural, paired with a sound cue and a hit-stop, in a different colour and shape; never the donor's frames

briefs.label: Step-shove on guard (own label)
briefs.why: Pressing into a guard pushes the defender back and bounces the attacker a little. Reads as weight at 375 wide.
briefs.keep: Stepper recoils by half the step; defender moves by twice the step; only while boxes overlap
briefs.change: Shove depends on guard state and stamina (row 3), has a cap so no fighter is pushed off the stage, and uses our own timing; not the donor's numbers
